Fixed S-meter dBm scale, audio/FFT stream reconnect persistence, and WFView fallback timer for IC-7300 MK2
IC-7300 MK2 (CI-V addr 0xB6) does NOT send scope/waterfall data (cmd 0x27 sub 0x00) over USB CI-V serial, even when scope is displayed on radio LCD. WFView TCP is needed for waterfall data.
React StrictMode in dev causes mount→unmount→mount cycles that close/reopen WebSocket connections. Bridge must use grace period timers to keep streams alive across brief disconnects.
When session continuations happen after context compaction, code changes from previous sessions may NOT be persisted. Always verify fixes by reading the actual file before assuming they're applied.
rawSmeterToDbm scale: CI-V raw 0-120 maps to S0-S9 (-127 to -73 dBm), raw 121-241 maps to S9+1 to S9+60 (-72 to -13 dBm). BCD codec: d1=high byte (hundreds), d2=low byte (tens+units).
Frontend stream re-subscribe must happen AFTER radio:state confirms connection, not immediately on WS connect — bridge may not have rig controller ready yet on restart.

Tile engine debugging: fixed alignment rotation (Rx only, not Rx+Ry), switched from GIBS MODIS (cloudy daily photos) to ESRI World Imagery (cloud-free), fixed group transform via R3F group prop instead of useEffect
3d-tiles-renderer ECEF frame: +X=prime meridian, +Y=90E, +Z=north pole. Propulse frame: +X=prime meridian, +Y=north pole, +Z=90W. Only Rx(-PI/2) needed to align.
R3F TilesRenderer group transform must use the `group` prop (e.g. group={{scale:[...], rotation:[...]}}) not useEffect on tilesRef.current.group — R3F reconciler overwrites manual changes
NASA GIBS MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor shows real daily satellite imagery WITH clouds — unusable for apps needing clear geography
ESRI World Imagery tiles at server.arcgisonline.com are freely accessible with CORS, no API key, cloud-free satellite composite
TilesPlugin args can be object or array — object form is cleaner and matches README examples

Fixed 14+ globe overlay visibility bugs caused by 3d-tiles-renderer depth buffer occlusion, plus WSPR path AdditiveBlending issue, LayersPopover UX, weather radar blinking, alert flyout positioning, satellite footprint selection, and lightning visual upgrade.

3d-tiles-renderer creates tile meshes with depthWrite: true (Three.js default). Overlays at radii close to r=1.0 need depthTest: false to avoid being occluded by tile depth buffer. Working overlays (SpotCluster, BeaconNetwork, Satellites) already had this; broken ones did not.

depthTest: false makes overlays visible through the planet (translucent globe effect). Only use it for overlays that genuinely need to ignore depth (flat surface overlays at r≈1.0). Arcs that rise above the surface (WSPR at r=1.008-1.35) should keep depthTest: true.

AdditiveBlending makes thin lines invisible against bright backgrounds (satellite tile imagery). Lines only appear where background is dark (horizon edge against space). Switch to NormalBlending for overlays that must be visible against bright globe tiles.
For WSPR paths specifically: the fix was NormalBlending (not depthTest: false). depthTest: false caused see-through planet. The blending mode was the actual visibility issue, not depth testing.
renderOrder controls GPU submission order but does NOT override depth testing. An overlay with renderOrder: 11 still gets discarded if depthTest: true and depth buffer has closer values from tiles.
LineBasicMaterial in WebGL is always 1px wide regardless of lineWidth setting. For thicker screen-space lines, use drei's <Line> (Line2) which supports lineWidth in screen pixels.
When launching haiku sub-agents for file edits, verify changes actually persisted to disk — agent edits may not persist in isolated contexts. Always check git diff after agent completion.
